neutral_facts.value: The accused and the complainant were residents of the same village and owned adjacent agricultural lands. There was a dispute over the right of way to access their respective lands. On 04.10.2002, the accused attacked the complainant and his father with a cycle chain and stone, resulting in the father's death and the complainant's injuries. The complainant provided a detailed account of the incident, including the presence of multiple accused and the use of weapons. The medical evidence confirmed the nature and severity of the injuries, linking them to the use of cycle chain and stone. The trial court convicted the accused based on the eyewitness account, medical evidence, and recovery of weapons. The High Court affirmed the conviction.

The injuries on the body of P.W.4 were also noted, and the doctor stated that all injuries were ante-mortem in nature, caused by hard and blunt objects, including cycle chain and stones. witness_credibility.value: The court assessed that although there were discrepancies in P.W.4's evidence, his version was supported by medical evidence and the testimony of another eyewitness, P.W.5. The court found no reason to disbelieve his version in order to reject the prosecution's case.

quotes.text: The evidence of P.W.4 in every other respect fully supports his version in the complaint and which was also to a very great extent supported by the medical evidence and version of another eyewitness P.W.5, no reason to disbelieve his version in order to reject the case of the prosecution.
The conviction and sentence was affirmed by the High Court.
From the Judgment & Order dated 16.01.2006 of the High Court of Bombay at Aurangabad in Criminal Appeal No. 611 of 2003.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the conviction was based on the evidence of PW4, PW5, and medical evidence, which collectively established the involvement of the appellants in the crime, their common intention to eliminate the deceased, and the coordinated vengeance involved in the assault.

quotes.text: The evidence of P.W.4, read along with the version of P.W.5 and the other medical evidence, as well as the expert opinion, discloses the involvement of the appellants in the crime, apart from their common intention to eliminate the deceased, as well as P.W.4.

The medical evidence substantially establishes the intention of the accused to eliminate the deceased and the injuries sustained by the deceased discloses the coordinated vengeance with which the assault was caused by the appellants, in order to ensure that the deceased did not survive.

defence_argument.value: The defence contended that the conviction was mainly based on the sole eyewitness PW4, whose evidence had discrepancies, and that the trial court improperly relied on his testimony without proper corroboration. They also challenged the medical evidence and the bloodstain findings, arguing that the prosecution failed to establish these through independent evidence.

quotes.text: The conviction was mainly based on the sole eye-witness, P.W.4 and having regard to the various discrepancies in his evidence, he could not have been present and witnessed the incident.
The Trial Court without any supporting expert evidence concluded that the shirt of two accused contained human blood, which was not true.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the conviction and sentence were justified based on the combined evidence of PW4, PW5, and medical testimony, which demonstrated the involvement of the accused and their common intention to eliminate the deceased.

quotes.text: The conviction was not based on the solitary statement of P.W.4 alone, but was also supported by other eyewitness viz., P.W.5, whose evidence merited acceptance on par with the evidence of P.W.4, apart from the medical evidence fully supporting the case of the prosecution.

The medical evidence substantially establishes the intention of the accused to eliminate the deceased and the injuries sustained by the deceased discloses the coordinated vengeance with which the assault was caused by the appellants, in order to ensure that the deceased did not survive.
